Gap/Question: Modelo de propriedade e estrutura de conteúdo do Canvas fixado por canal (quem autora, aprova e mantém a regra/conhecimento vigente; taxonomia de canais por serviço) não está definido.
Impact/Notes: Bloqueador de design: sem esse modelo, o Canvas corre o risco de reproduzir o mesmo conhecimento disperso e desatualizado que a epic pretende substituir. Já sinalizado como open item no Discovery Brief e como [assumption] nos kb_sources da epic.

Gap/Question: As 1.800 licenças Slack Enterprise Plus já validadas cobrem a Sala de Situação (monitoramento digital), não o headcount real de atendentes nos 244 postos físicos + 900 totens de autoatendimento que esta epic pretende colocar no Slack.
Impact/Notes: Risco direto de dimensionamento e custo de licenciamento incremental; sem esse número, `estimate`/`commercials` não conseguem validar cobertura de licença para o rollout da Fase 1. Confirmado pelo usuário como não dimensionado ainda.

Gap/Question: Escopo real do piloto (qual posto, quantos atendentes, quais serviços) está totalmente aberto — os nomes citados (Ana, Anderson, Felipe, Santo Amaro, CIN) são storyboard do material de venda, não um piloto combinado com a Prodesp.
Impact/Notes: Sem posto/serviço/headcount definidos, a epic não tem unidade de medida para sizing, sequenciamento de rollout ou critério de sucesso do piloto.

Gap/Question: O workflow de 'roteamento de casos para postos com capacidade ociosa' não define o critério de capacidade ociosa (fila, tempo médio de atendimento, disponibilidade do atendente) nem a fonte de dados que alimenta essa decisão.
Impact/Notes: Sem critério objetivo, o roteamento entre postos vira julgamento manual do atendente, esvaziando o valor de automação citado no objetivo de negócio (visibilidade de capacidade ociosa sem contratar gente nova).

Gap/Question: O 'huddle com especialista sem sair da cadeira' não identifica quem é o especialista (outro atendente sênior, back-office Prodesp, suporte de sistema, ou Salesforce) nem o SLA/disponibilidade esperada desse papel.
Impact/Notes: Sem essa definição, o desenho de escalonamento por huddle não tem persona de destino nem expectativa de tempo de resposta — afeta diretamente a promessa de reduzir o tempo de 'preciso de ajuda' até o cidadão atendido.

Gap/Question: O 'workflow de aviso quando um sistema cai' (contingência) não especifica a fonte do sinal de indisponibilidade (monitoramento automático de sistema legado, ou relato manual do atendente) nem o canal/audiência do broadcast.
Impact/Notes: Sem fonte de sinal definida, o workflow de contingência depende de detecção manual, o que reduz a velocidade de resposta que a epic promete resolver (hoje: atendente levanta, usa celular pessoal ou pede para voltar).

Gap/Question: A premissa de design de que nenhum dado biométrico bruto trafegará nos canais de texto do Slack (apenas relato textual do problema) ainda não é um controle implementado — é uma intenção a validar.
Impact/Notes: Risco de compliance LGPD/segurança se o controle não for tecnicamente reforçado (ex.: DLP, guardrail de Agentforce) e depender apenas de disciplina do atendente. Relevante porque a coordenação institucional em Slack é a proposta de valor central de LGPD desta epic.

Gap/Question: Guardrails formais do agente Agentforce-em-canal (papel, dados acessíveis, ações permitidas, o que ele não deve fazer) ainda não foram definidos para o caso de uso do guichê — o framework de 5 atributos e o risco de 'revelar PII a usuário não autenticado' (padrão nomeado em `knowledge/staar-agentforce-governance-guardrails.md`) ainda não foi aplicado a este agente.
Impact/Notes: Sem guardrails formais, o agente em contexto de atendimento (dúvidas do próprio fluxo) corre o mesmo risco de vazamento de PII/dados sensíveis nomeado como failure mode padrão da Salesforce PS para agentes Agentforce. [extends: staar-agentforce-governance-guardrails.md]

Gap/Question: Owner de governança de agentes de IA do lado Prodesp ainda não identificado — quem aprova o conteúdo do Canvas, quem monitora o comportamento do Agentforce em canal, quem responde por incidentes de guardrail.
Impact/Notes: Confirmado pelo usuário como não identificado ainda. Mais crítico à medida que o Agentforce entra em contexto de atendimento real (não apenas monitoramento), mesmo na Fase 1 tática.

Gap/Question: Governança/Centro de Excelência (CoE) ou função de change management para a operação contínua do posto de trabalho Slack — política de canais, ciclo de vida de canais por serviço, versionamento do Canvas — está em escopo desta epic/SOW, ou é responsabilidade do cliente (Prodesp)?
Impact/Notes: Pergunta de disciplina voltada ao comprador. Governança e adoção (papéis, treinamento, política de canais) já foram confirmadas em escopo pelo usuário no discovery, mas a estrutura operacional contínua (quem mantém depois do go-live) ainda não foi detalhada. Ver `knowledge/staar-agentforce-governance-guardrails.md` (modelo de CoE) como referência, se o cliente optar por trazer isso para dentro do escopo.

Gap/Question: Pesquisa de experiência do usuário / desenho de serviço (UX research / service design) para o novo posto de trabalho do atendente — uma superfície de trabalho diária inteiramente nova, substituindo ferramentas e conhecimento hoje dispersos — está em escopo desta epic, ou o desenho de canais/Canvas/huddle será feito sem validação direta com atendentes reais?
Impact/Notes: Pergunta de disciplina voltada ao comprador. Sem esse trabalho, o desenho de canais-por-serviço, estrutura de Canvas e fluxo de huddle corre risco de não refletir o comportamento real do atendente no guichê, ameaçando adoção.

Gap/Question: Identidade dos sistemas legados citados no diagrama de arquitetura-alvo (T7, Sistema Semântico, 'Atendimento') não está resolvida. O usuário decidiu deprioritizar o fechamento do T7 no discovery, mas sinalizou que seria bom resolver antes do desenho técnico da Fase 1 especificamente.
Impact/Notes: Ainda que a integração pesada com esses sistemas seja majoritariamente Fase 2 (MuleSoft), o material cita 'T7' como fonte de dúvidas dentro do próprio fluxo de atendimento do guichê (Fase 1) — se o Agentforce-em-canal precisar consultar esse sistema, a identidade não resolvida bloqueia o design técnico, não apenas o discovery.

Gap/Question: Champion/patrocinador executivo da Balcão V2 no lado Prodesp ainda não identificado — diferente da Frente A de licenças (que tem Thiago Waltz como ponto de entrada).
Impact/Notes: Risco de prontidão do cliente: sem patrocinador executivo claro para o piloto tático, decisões de escopo de piloto (posto, serviço, headcount — ver G0103) e adoção de política de canais podem ficar sem dono do lado do cliente.

Gap/Question: Documento de posicionamento LGPD/Trust sobre localização de inferência do Agentforce — existência confirmada pelo usuário, mas sem documento/URL específico localizado ou citável; pesquisa web dedicada não encontrou orientação pública substituta.
Impact/Notes: Se a epic depender de afirmar postura de compliance sobre onde a inferência de IA ocorre (relevante dado que o agente estará em contexto de atendimento real, não apenas monitoramento), esse gap precisa ser fechado com o time de conta antes de qualquer entregável cliente-facing assumir postura de compliance.

Gap/Question: O material de venda de origem (BSA) não detalha como o atendente sinaliza start/end de um caso dentro do canal (abertura/fechamento de thread, status do atendimento) — não há modelo de ciclo de vida do 'caso' dentro do canal Slack.
Impact/Notes: Sem esse modelo, fica ambíguo como medir o objetivo de negócio citado (reduzir tempo do 'preciso de ajuda' até a cidadã ser atendida) — não há evento de início/fim claro a instrumentar.

Gap/Question: No real-time capacity signal source has been identified for any of the 244 postos or 900 totens. Discovery describes the desired outcome ("Redirecionamento dinâmico: elimine filas em postos superlotados utilizando a capacidade ociosa de retaguarda de outras unidades") but names no system, feed, or manual process that reports which postos/attendants/totens are idle right now. The epic's kb_sources field already flags this as an assumption — no KB document covers a workforce-availability or queue-state data source for this account.
Impact/Notes: This is the load-bearing dependency for the entire epic: without a capacity signal, there is nothing to route against. Until a source is named (existing SF/PRODESP system, new instrumentation, or manual self-report in Slack), E03 cannot be designed, sized, or built — it can only be assumed. Should be treated as a pre-build blocker for Fase 1, not a detail to resolve during build.

Gap/Question: If no automated capacity signal exists, the only fallback is attendants self-reporting availability/idle status manually inside Slack (e.g., a status field, a channel post, a Canvas toggle). This turns a systems-integration capability into a change-management and adoption problem, and the signal quality degrades if attendants don't self-report consistently.
Impact/Notes: Risk to the outcome metric ("sem necessidade de contratar mais atendentes") — a stale or gamed manual signal could route cases to postos that are not actually idle, defeating the purpose. Adoption/governance already confirmed in scope per the discovery brief, but this specific mechanic (manual capacity self-report) has not been named or agreed with the client.

Gap/Question: "Capacidade ociosa" is undefined operationally. Is it: (a) attendant headcount currently unassigned, (b) queue length/wait time per posto, (c) service-type-specific availability (idle for CNH but saturated for CIN), or (d) totem throughput/availability? The epic description bundles postos and totens together but totens are self-service kiosks, not staffed capacity — their role in a "capacity" model is unclear.
Impact/Notes: Without a definition, there is no way to size the data model, the routing logic, or the UI surface (what an attendant sees when deciding to route a case). Blocks design and estimation.

Gap/Question: The two source decks describe two different "idle capacity" mechanics that could both plausibly be what E03 means: Corte 1 (Jackson) describes an idle colleague joining a huddle/conference for specialist escalation at the same case ('o colega ocioso do outro posto' backing up the current attendant); Corte 2 (Vinicius) describes 'Felipe,' an idle attendant elsewhere, pulling entire cases for remote document validation before or instead of an in-person visit. E03's description ('roteamento de casos entre os 244 postos + 900 totens, direcionando demanda para onde há capacidade ociosa') does not specify which of these two mechanics — augment-in-place via huddle, or reassign-the-case-elsewhere — it is building.
Impact/Notes: These imply materially different technical builds (presence-aware huddle routing vs. case/queue reassignment across postos) and different governance/LGPD handling (case data crossing posto boundaries vs. staying local). Needs client confirmation before design; currently assumed to be case-reassignment based on the epic's own wording ("roteamento de casos"), but that reading conflicts with the Corte 1 huddle framing in the same source material.

Gap/Question: The stated business objective — "sem necessidade de contratar mais atendentes" — has no baseline. Current idle-time rate per posto, current overflow/queue-abandonment rate, and current headcount distribution across the 244 postos are all unknown. The discovery brief explicitly flags the cited wait-time KPIs (15/16/17 min) as illustrative and unvalidated by the client.
Impact/Notes: Without a baseline, the outcome cannot be measured (no before/after), and no metric block can be attached to this capability without inventing numbers. Relevant to `design`/`estimate` sizing and to any success-criteria language in the SOW.

Gap/Question: No decision rule is defined for when a case should be routed to another posto's idle capacity versus handled locally (e.g., distance/travel burden to the citizen if it means physical redirection, service-type match, case complexity threshold, SLA/wait-time trigger).
Impact/Notes: Needed to scope the routing logic itself; without it, "routing" is a label with no algorithm behind it. Also affects whether this is rules-based (Flow/Omni-Channel-style) or requires a more complex matching/queueing engine.

Gap/Question: The role of the 900 self-service totens in this epic is unspecified. Are totens a demand source that triggers routing (e.g., a totem detects it cannot resolve a case and needs to signal an idle human elsewhere), a capacity sink (idle totens absorb simple cases redirected from crowded counters), both, or neither — with "totens" in the epic description simply inherited from the corrected volumetria figure (244 postos + 900 totens) rather than a deliberate scope choice?
Impact/Notes: If totens have no real role in this capability, the epic description overstates scope inherited from a volumetria correction (see discovery brief) rather than a discovery finding. Needs a scope-narrowing confirmation or a concrete totem-routing requirement.

Gap/Question: The discovery brief's Open Questions already flag a Slack license sizing gap: 1,800 Slack Enterprise Plus licenses are validated for the Sala de Situação (digital-channel monitoring), not for attendant headcount across the 244 postos. E03's routing mechanic depends on idle attendants being reachable/visible inside Slack across the whole network — but if attendant headcount at the 244 postos exceeds validated licensing, the capability has no user base to route into.
Impact/Notes: Direct blocker specific to E03 (more so than to other Fase 1 epics, since routing requires network-wide attendant presence, not just single-posto usage). Needs headcount-vs-license reconciliation with the client before Fase 1 design is finalized.

Gap/Question: Real-time capacity signaling across 244 physical postos assumes reliable network/device connectivity at each site. No discovery source addresses infrastructure state (connectivity, device availability, uptime) at the counter level across the network.
Impact/Notes: If connectivity is inconsistent at a meaningful share of postos, a real-time signal (whichever source is eventually named per G0301) may be unreliable exactly where it's most needed (busy/overloaded sites). Worth a discovery question before committing to a real-time (vs. near-real-time/batch) design.

Gap/Question: A capacity/idle-time signal that surfaces which attendants are not currently busy is, functionally, individual performance/utilization monitoring data. Combined with the fact that no AI/data governance owner has been identified on the PRODESP side (per the discovery brief's Open Questions) and that current cross-posto coordination is informally described as happening "fora da LGPD," there is a labor-relations and data-governance exposure in formalizing an idle-time signal without an agreed policy on how that data is used, retained, and who sees it.
Impact/Notes: Could surface as a stakeholder/union sensitivity during rollout even if technically compliant. Should be raised with the client's HR/governance stakeholders before broad deployment, not discovered during pilot.

Gap/Question: The epic assumes routing is achievable without new headcount purely by better visibility/redistribution of existing idle time. This assumes idle time is (a) real and material in volume across the network, and (b) fungible — i.e., an idle attendant at Posto B can actually perform work originating from Posto A's case (same systems access, same service-type training/certification, same authority to act on another unit's citizen record).
Impact/Notes: If service-type specialization or system-access boundaries prevent cross-posto case handling, the epic's core premise (idle capacity is interchangeable) breaks down regardless of whether a capacity signal exists. Worth validating with an operations stakeholder, not just a technical one.

Gap/Question: Has any experience/service design discipline (UX research, service design, or content design) been engaged to define how a case-routing/reassignment moment is actually experienced by the citizen (if it involves any wait or hand-off) and by the receiving idle attendant (case handoff context, continuity of the citizen's history)? No such discipline signal appears in discovery for this epic.
Impact/Notes: Routing changes who serves the citizen and how continuity is preserved across a hand-off — a service-design/UX gap here risks a technically-working capability that citizens or attendants experience as confusing or worse than today's workaround (personal WhatsApp groups).

Gap/Question: Who on the PRODESP side owns governance for a cross-posto capacity/routing data model — i.e., a data steward or CoE function accountable for how idle-time/case-routing data is defined, who can see it, and how change requests to the routing logic are governed over time? The discovery brief already notes no AI-governance owner has been identified account-wide; this asks specifically whether a narrower data-stewardship owner exists for this capability's data.
Impact/Notes: Without a named owner, routing-logic changes and capacity-signal definitions risk drifting informally (mirroring today's ungoverned WhatsApp-group workaround this epic is meant to replace).

Gap/Question: E03 is scoped under Fase 1 (tactical, no heavy integration), yet the Fase 2 deck's "Felipe" idle-attendant mechanic — remote document validation triggered by pre-service WhatsApp outreach — depends on the same underlying idle-capacity concept and is explicitly Fase 2 (MuleSoft-integrated) scope per `decisions/0002`. It is not clear whether Fase 1's E03 is meant to build a standalone, lighter version of capacity visibility/routing that Fase 2 later extends, or whether E03's real design only becomes coherent once Fase 2's remote-validation mechanic exists.
Impact/Notes: Affects roadmap sequencing and whether E03 can be considered complete/valuable on its own in Fase 1, or is really a foundation piece whose payoff only lands in Fase 2. Relevant to `roadmap` and `design` phasing decisions.

Gap/Question: There is no defined specialist directory or routing logic mapping an escalation trigger (biometric failure, document mismatch, out-of-Canvas question) to the correct specialist domain (Detran, IIRGD, Instituto da Identidade, TI, etc.). The epic's own kb_sources tag this as '[assumption: a definir em design]'.
Impact/Notes: Without this, the huddle mechanism has no way to route a case to the right specialist channel — the attendant either guesses or the design must hard-code a manual channel-per-issue-type mapping before build. Blocks E02 design and any staffing/on-call conversation with the specialist-owning institutions.

Gap/Question: No specialist availability / on-call model is defined. The mechanic assumes a specialist is reachable in real time ("entra em huddle... resolvida em minutos"), but there is no confirmed staffing model, coverage hours, or fallback path for when no specialist answers the huddle request.
Impact/Notes: If a huddle goes unanswered, the citizen is back to 'volte depois' — the exact failure state the epic claims to fix. Needs a defined SLA + escalation-of-escalation path (e.g., queue, secondary specialist, or supervisor) before this can be presented as reliably faster than today's WhatsApp workaround.

Gap/Question: The epic's core value claim is that this replaces WhatsApp coordination that is 'fora da LGPD — sem histórico, sem auditoria' with an auditable, institutional channel. The source material confirms the Slack ticket and channel are logged and auditable, but does not confirm whether the huddle itself (a live voice call) is recorded, transcribed, or otherwise retained. If the specialist's actual guidance is only spoken and not captured, the audit-trail claim holds for 'a request was made and a ticket exists' but not for 'what was actually said/advised.'
Impact/Notes: This is the load-bearing LGPD claim for the whole epic. If huddle audio isn't retained, the compliance narrative to PRODESP needs to be scoped down to 'auditable request trail,' not 'auditable coordination' — unless Slack huddle recording/transcription is explicitly designed in.

Gap/Question: The source material flags that the Flex Credit cost of the ticket/huddle-opening step is 40 Flex if triggered by Agentforce classic, but jumps to a different (200 Flex) measure if the channel 'door' is a Slackbot instead — and the source itself says this ambiguity 'não é medição desta conta' (not yet resolved). It is unresolved which mechanism (Slackbot vs. Agentforce classic) actually opens the ticket/huddle in this design.
Impact/Notes: This is a build-time and cost-model fork, not just a documentation nuance: Slackbot and Agentforce-classic are different implementation paths with different Flex consumption. Needs resolution before `design`/`estimate` treat E02's automation mechanism as settled.

Gap/Question: The discovery brief states a design premise that no raw biometric data should transit Slack text channels — but a huddle is a live voice call, and the walkthrough example has the specialist verbally referencing the citizen's specific case and biometric collection issue in real time. No guardrail is defined for what a specialist may or may not say/ask about the citizen verbally during a huddle.
Impact/Notes: The text-channel guardrail does not automatically extend to voice; if unaddressed, the epic could introduce a PII/LGPD exposure path in exactly the channel (huddle) it introduces to fix governance. Needs an explicit guardrail statement in design, per the STAAR governance framework's People/Business/Technology/Data lens.

Gap/Question: Detran, IIRGD, and Instituto da Identidade are separate government entities from PRODESP, not PRODESP staff. No identity/access model is defined for how their specialists join a huddle inside PRODESP's Slack Enterprise Plus org — as licensed guest users, via Slack Connect, or some other cross-agency provisioning path.
Impact/Notes: Slack Connect / external-guest provisioning has its own licensing, governance, and security review implications that are absent from any discovery source. This is a capability/architecture gap that affects both E02's design and E05's governance scope, and should be resolved before any pilot posto is chosen.

Gap/Question: It is unclear whether the huddle is always manually initiated by the attendant, or whether Agentforce can also proactively suggest/trigger the huddle when its own suggested fixes fail. The Canvas-lookup step and the huddle-open step read as sequential in the walkthrough, but the actual trigger UX (button, slash command, natural-language request) is undefined.
Impact/Notes: Affects the attendant-facing UX design and the Agentforce action definition (Role/Actions per the 5-attributes framework) — needs to be pinned down in `design`, not left implicit.

Gap/Question: The only concretely described 'foge do script' trigger scenario is the CIN biometric-capture failure (explicitly labeled storyboard). No taxonomy exists yet of the full set of escalation-trigger categories across other Poupatempo service lines (CNH, exames, etc.) that E02's routing table would need to cover.
Impact/Notes: Without this taxonomy, the specialist-directory/routing design (G0201) can only be scoped for one illustrative service, not sized for the pilot's actual service mix. Needed before `requirements`/`design` can size E02 realistically.

Gap/Question: No validated SLA or target resolution time exists for the huddle escalation path. The deck's framing ('resolvida em minutos') and the 15/16/17-minute wait-time KPIs elsewhere in the material are both explicitly flagged in the discovery brief as illustrative/unvalidated, not a client-confirmed baseline.
Impact/Notes: Any success metric or before/after claim for E02 in a client-facing artifact must carry the illustrative-KPI caveat already established in the discovery brief; do not let a future `design`/`narratives` pass silently promote these numbers to fact.

Gap/Question: [Experience design discipline gap] Has the citizen-facing experience during an active huddle been mapped? The attendant is on a live voice call with a specialist while the citizen stands at the counter — what does the citizen see/hear, and has the attendant's simultaneous cognitive load (monitoring Canvas + huddle + citizen) been validated through service design or UX research, rather than assumed from the storyboard alone?
Impact/Notes: Signal only, not a mandate — but the storyboard is explicitly illustrative, so the actual in-huddle citizen and attendant experience is unvalidated. Worth raising to the client as a discovery question before pilot design locks the interaction pattern.

Gap/Question: [Governance discipline gap] Who, on the PRODESP side, owns and maintains the specialist directory and routing rules over time (as specialist orgs, staffing, or regulations change)? The project's own open questions note that no AI-governance owner has been identified yet, and E02's routing logic would need an accountable steward once built, not just a one-time design decision.
Impact/Notes: Signal only, not a mandate — but without an owner, the routing table designed in E02 has no maintenance path and will drift out of date. Worth raising as a buyer-facing question alongside the broader AI-governance-owner gap already logged in the discovery brief's Open Questions.

Gap/Question: The Flex Credit consumption model for the escalation mechanic (40 vs. 200 Flex per request, per G0204) rests partly on an unconfirmed internal committee remark that the account's Flex allocation is 'ilimitado' — the discovery brief explicitly treats that as a hypothesis, not a fact of the Digital Wallet contract.
Impact/Notes: If huddle/ticket volume scales across 244 postos and the 'unlimited Flex' assumption is wrong, there is a real cost-exposure risk behind this specific automation mechanic. Relevant to `estimate`/`commercials` sizing, not just design.

Gap/Question: The walkthrough example has the specialist give verbal, step-by-step device instructions with no screen-share, device-diagnostic, or system-state visibility for the specialist — purely voice-guided. No design decision confirms whether this verbal-only model is sufficient for more complex hardware/system failures beyond the biometric-capture example.
Impact/Notes: For simple procedural fixes, voice-only may be adequate; for a genuine system outage or hardware fault, it may not be — worth flagging as a design boundary question rather than assuming voice-only huddle covers every escalation case E02 is meant to handle.

Gap/Question: The source deck's own visual implies the outage-broadcast workflow is triggered by automated detection of a system going down (Workflow Builder fires on a 'Sistema fora — Ativo' event), but the Discovery Brief commits Phase 1 to 'nenhuma integração pesada nova' — no new integration into Detran, IIRGD, or other backend systems. Without a monitoring integration, nothing exists to auto-detect the outage; the workflow's actual trigger must be a human declaring the outage (e.g., filling a form or posting in a channel), which is a materially different (and less complete) mechanism than the deck depicts.
Impact/Notes: This is the single most load-bearing ambiguity in E04 — it determines whether the build is a simple manual-trigger Slack workflow (small, no-code) or implies a monitoring/integration dependency that Phase 1 has explicitly ruled out. Must be resolved before design/estimate; if left as-is, the acceptance criteria risk overstating what a no-integration Phase 1 can actually detect.

Gap/Question: No role or permission model is defined for who is authorized to declare a system-down event and activate the contingency broadcast (a supervisor? any attendant? a designated ops channel owner?). Absent this, the workflow has no gate against false or duplicate activations across 244+ postos.
Impact/Notes: Needed for both the build (who can trigger the Workflow Builder flow) and for adoption/training (E05) — an unrestricted trigger risks alert fatigue or conflicting simultaneous declarations from multiple postos.

Gap/Question: The epic description names 'sistema do Detran' only as an example ('ex.:') of a critical system whose outage should trigger the workflow. No enumerated list of which systems qualify (Detran, IIRGD, biometria estadual, Sistema Semântico, T7, 'Atendimento' — several of these identities are themselves still open per the Discovery Brief) exists to scope what this workflow must cover.
Impact/Notes: Without a confirmed system list, build scope for 'quais sistemas disparam contingência' is undefined — risks scope creep (every system outage expected to trigger this) or under-coverage (a critical system left out).

Gap/Question: The deck states today's core pain as 'ninguém sabe se é local ou geral' (nobody knows if an outage is local to one posto or systemwide) — but the described solution broadcasts the same alert to '100% dos postos' unconditionally, regardless of whether the underlying outage is local or general. No design decision confirms whether the workflow needs to scope/segment the broadcast (by região, by service, or by confirmed blast radius) or whether an always-global broadcast is an acceptable answer to the stated problem.
Impact/Notes: If the real driver is knowing scope of impact, and the design just floods every posto every time, the stated pain may not actually be resolved — worth confirming with the client whether blanket broadcast is sufficient or a targeted/graduated alert is expected.

Gap/Question: The deck states 'postos confirmam a contingência' as a key benefit ('Confirmações em tempo real'), but no UI mechanism is specified (a Slack button, emoji reaction, a form) nor is there any defined escalation or reminder path for a posto that never confirms receipt within a time window.
Impact/Notes: Without a confirmation mechanic and a non-response escalation path, the claimed 'segundos' reaction-time metric (itself unconfirmed, see G0410) has no operational teeth — a posto could simply never acknowledge and no one would know.

Gap/Question: Every source passage describes only the 'system goes down → broadcast alert + contingency plan' half of the flow. No stand-down / resolution step is described — how postos are told the outage is over and to resume normal procedure, and whether that requires the same declaring authority as the original trigger (see G0402).
Impact/Notes: Without a resolution/stand-down flow, postos have no defined signal to exit contingency mode, risking prolonged unnecessary workaround procedures after the underlying system is actually back up.

Gap/Question: Discovery notes explicitly name a sibling initiative, 'Sala de Situação' (Service Cloud, alerting when the citizen-facing channel goes down), as 'outro recorte, outro contrato' — a different scope, different contract from this SOW. Yet both initiatives are fundamentally 'system/channel is down, notify people' mechanics, on different clouds (Slack Workflow Builder here vs. Service Cloud there), for a shared underlying event class (a Prodesp system outage) that could affect both the attendant-facing and citizen-facing sides simultaneously.
Impact/Notes: Risk of duplicated, uncoordinated, or conflicting outage signals if both initiatives eventually run — worth an explicit boundary statement in the SOW/design (E04 owns attendant-facing broadcast only; Sala de Situação is out of this contract) so the client doesn't expect the two to be integrated with each other.

Gap/Question: PRODESP operates 244-246 physical postos; fanning a single outage declaration out to '100% dos postos' via Slack Workflow Builder in 'segundos' has not been validated against Slack Workflow Builder/API throughput or delivery-latency behavior at that fan-out scale.
Impact/Notes: If the pilot's single-posto proof-of-concept doesn't get load-tested at full-network fan-out before general rollout, the 'segundos' claim (already flagged as a hypothesis, G0410) could fail silently at scale — worth a scale-validation step in the pilot plan.
